text:
Sam Chen: Hey team — urgent P1. Customer org_acme_123 hit a negative balance after a partial chargeback on invoice inv_2026_04_02. They had legacy trial credits (promo_TRIAL_2024) that appear to have been clawed back twice. Their production traffic is blocked by billing limits; API calls return 402/403. Billing ref cb_78910. @Priya Nair @Alex Rivera please advise.

Priya Nair: Thanks Sam. Can you paste the invoice/ledger snapshot and the exact customer-facing error? Also, is this the legacy 'trial' flow we migrated in March?

Sam Chen: Customer error is: "Error 402 Payment Required: negative_balance" then some clients see "403 Forbidden: account suspended due to outstanding balance". Repro timeline: customer initiated chargeback/refund 2026-04-02, we processed refund on 2026-04-02, clawback job ran 2026-04-03 and removed trial credit, then a chargeback reversal processed 2026-04-04 which triggered another clawback -> net double clawback. Ledger snippet: 
```
ledger_entry 2026-04-02: +$50 promo_TRIAL_2024
ledger_entry 2026-04-03: -$50 trial_credit_clawback (cb_78910)
ledger_entry 2026-04-04: -$50 trial_credit_clawback (cb_78910_retry)
ledger_entry 2026-04-04: +$50 refund_processed (cb_78910)
balance: -$50
```

Alex Rivera: Assigning to billing eng to triage. @Jordan Kim can you check clawback job logs for org_acme_123 between 2026-04-03 and 2026-04-04? This smells like an idempotency/retry race.

Jordan Kim: On it. Quick note: the clawback worker subscribes to refunds.processed events and retries on transient failures — we had a spike in the event stream on 2026-04-04 and duplications are possible. Grepping now.

Jordan Kim: Found duplicates. Excerpt from logs: 
```
[2026-04-03T03:12:11Z] event_id=evt_aa11 refunds.processed cb_78910 applied clawback -50 for org_acme_123
[2026-04-04T01:05:02Z] event_id=evt_aa11_retry refunds.processed cb_78910 applied clawback -50 for org_acme_123
[2026-04-04T01:05:03Z] refund rollback processed +50 refund_processed cb_78910
```
Looks like event_id wasn't enforced as unique so second delivery applied a second clawback.

Priya Nair: Ok — short term we need a manual ledger fix and a mitigation so the customer can resume. Sam, does the customer want immediate restoration? We should also temporarily lift the billing threshold so API calls succeed while we fix ledger.

Sam Chen: They want restore ASAP, their app is in prod and customers are impacted. Please do manual credit + temp-lift. I'll draft a customer note.

Alex Rivera: I'll open an internal billing incident and perform a manual adjustment: add manual_credit +$50, tag support_restore, and set a short-term billing hold override for org_acme_123.

Jordan Kim: I've made a manual DB dedupe for those duplicate events (marked evt_aa11_retry as duplicate) and re-ran reconciliation for org_acme_123. Also opened a hotfix PR to enforce event_id uniqueness in the clawback worker before applying changes. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/billing/PR-3421 (hotfix, tests included). Aim to deploy within ~2h.

Priya Nair: Action items: 1) Alex apply manual +$50 credit and billing override (in progress). 2) Jordan deploy hotfix and confirm reconciliation. 3) Sam send customer-facing note and confirm restore. I'll own follow-up and postmortem. :thumbsup:

Sam Chen: Manual credit applied and override enabled — customer confirmed API calls are back to normal. Sent brief note: "we identified the issue and restored your credits; full postmortem to follow". They said thanks.

Jordan Kim: After dedupe + reconcile logs show final ledger: 
```
ledger_entry final: +$50 manual_credit support_restore
ledger_balance final: $0
```
Hotfix merged to release branch, will roll to prod in canary tonight.

Priya Nair: I'll file the postmortem and include mitigation checklist (idempotency checks, alert for duplicate clawback events, automatic reconciliation alert if balance < -10).

Sam Chen: Thanks all — closing once postmortem page is linked to the customer ticket. Good catch on the event dedupe.
